transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-02 14:30 PDT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood Product), Aisha (Lead ML Eng, Heliotrope), Tom (CTO), Priya (Head of Compliance), Evan (Platform Eng)
Links mentioned: deck (shorturl/redwood-json-demo), pilot spreadsheet (shorturl/redwood-pilot-spreadsheet), SOC2 pack (shorturl/redwood-soc2)

Summary (auto): quick walkthrough of JSON Mode and function-calling guardrails; customer wants pilot to validate structured extraction and safe tool invocations inside a VPC. High interest in Dedicated for predictable latency, compliance questions flagged by Priya. Agreed next steps and pilot plan items.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya with Redwood, AE on your account. Quick intros?
[00:12] Tom: Tom Barlow, CTO at Heliotrope, hi.
[00:15] Aisha: Aisha, ML lead.
[00:17] Priya: Priya, compliance.
[00:19] Evan: Evan, platform.
[00:22] Daniel: Daniel Park, SE, I'll run through the technical demo.
[00:27] Maya: Perfect. We'll do a short context / goals then Daniel will demo JSON Mode and tool calling with our Console and Optimize suggestions.
[00:35] Tom: Our main goal is a proof that we can extract structured clinical trial metadata from free text and then call internal tools for staging and validation, and do it inside our compliance constraints. Latency needs to be consistent for UI flows.
[00:48] Daniel: Great. We'll focus on schema-enforced outputs — JSON Mode — plus safe tool calling with typed contracts. I'll show the Console for setting up fallbacks, and Optimize for quantization/batching recommendations.
[01:12] [demo starts/screenshare noise] Daniel: Alright I'm sharing the Console. Up top you'll see Model Catalog — for the pilot we recommend a mid-sized open model variant with a Dedicated pool; it keeps latency consistent.
[01:36] Aisha: Quick Q, when you say "Dedicated pool", you mean reserved GPUs that only our requests hit?
[01:40] Daniel: Yes. "Dedicated capacity" = your reserved GPU pool with predictable throughput and isolation. You get routing policies, and you can pin model versions. Autoscaling is configurable, we can attach burst capacity but it's controlled by policies.
[01:50] Priya: From a compliance point, we need VPC connectivity, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs. Also retention controls.
[01:57] Lina: Yes — Private deployment supports customer-managed VPC and KMS/HSM integrations. Audit logs and token-level tracing are available in the Console. We can show sample network diagrams.
[02:10] Evan: Ok, if we go Private, will we still get Optimize recommendations?
[02:14] Daniel: Yes. Optimize is a toolkit that runs recommendations based on observed workload; for Private deployments it's an agent that submits anonymized telemetry per your policy — you can opt out of sharing. The suggestions (batch sizes, quantization profile) can be applied locally.
[02:30] Aisha: Show the JSON Mode flow please.
[02:33] Daniel: On the right is the Runtime -> JSON Mode tab. You can supply a JSON schema and the runtime will enforce type/field constraints, plus it can auto-correct near-miss tokens. I'll paste a sample schema for clinical_trial_metadata.
[02:50] [typing] Daniel: Example: {"trial_id": "string","start_date":"date","arm_definitions":[{"arm_id":"string","description":"string","eligibility_criteria":"string"}],"primary_outcome":"string"} — send that as the schema.
[03:10] Maya: Note: schema enforcement means the model is constrained to produce valid JSON. If it fails, the runtime can attempt structured repair or run fallback parsing.
[03:23] Aisha: That repair step — is it automatic? I want deterministic behavior for our pipeline.
[03:28] Daniel: You can configure auto-repair off, and instead redirect to a fallback model or to a synchronous parser tool. We recommend a canary fallback model with a higher temperature = lower hallucination? (laughs) — sorry, I mean lower temperature.
[03:48] Tom: And what's the cost implication of enabling JSON Mode + repair?
[03:52] Maya: Repair attempts count as extra tokens if they re-run generation. Optimize can estimate token cost per request across configured fallbacks; we'll include a sample cost projection in the pilot spreadsheet.
[04:10] Priya: The tool-calling piece — we have internal services that do PII scrubbing and validation. How does Redwood call customer tools safely?
[04:22] Daniel: We support typed function signatures that map to your internal APIs. Calls can be proxied through Private Deployments so payloads never leave your VPC. You can also configure sanitizer hooks: either a pre-call lambda in your network or a Redwood-run sandbox with RBAC.
[04:40] Evan: For proxying, do we need to open inbound ports to Redwood?
[04:44] Lina: No inbound: the Private agent in your VPC makes outbound to the Redwood control plane over an approved egress path, or if you're fully air-gapped we can run an on-prem package that keeps the control plane local.
[04:58] Aisha: Show an example of a function call binding to the schema.
[05:02] Daniel: Sure. Here's a function signature in the Console: validate_trial(trial_json: object) -> {status: string, errors: [string]} — it's typed. When JSON Mode returns the trial_json, the runtime can call validate_trial, and the response becomes part of the overall response object.
[05:23] [00:05 background mutter] Daniel: The Console shows success/failure traces per invocation, tracing token counts and latency.
[05:33] Tom: What about fallback orchestration? Example: if primary model times out, go to smaller local model?
[05:38] Daniel: Exactly. Smart routing policies let you pick fallback chains: e.g., Hosted -> Dedicated -> Local quantized model. You can pick policies by latency SLO, cost, or region. The runtime automatically re-routes failing requests according to policy.
[05:58] Aisha: We want deterministic outputs for downstream validation. How do you ensure schema stability across model versions?
[06:05] Daniel: Pin a model version in the Route config and use rollout policies to canary new versions. Also you can set evaluation prompt sets so Optimize monitors quality regressions tied to your test suite and triggers alerts.
[06:20] Priya: For auditing, we need token-level logs and immutable records for inbound prompts and tool calls. Is that supported?
[06:26] Lina: Yes — audit logs include call graphs, timestamps, and hashes of payloads if you want to avoid storing raw content. We can sign logs with HSM keys.
[06:40] Evan: Latency numbers? We need <250ms p95 for our UI path.
[06:44] Daniel: For a Dedicated pool with midsize model and continuous batching disabled for low-latency routes, we typically see 80–180ms p95 depending on sequence length. We'll run a benchmark for your actual sequences in pilot.
[07:02] Maya: We'll also show Optimize's batching suggestions — it will recommend whether to enable micro-batching for throughput vs latency tradeoff.
[07:12] Aisha: What about KV cache for repeated context? We often have long patient histories and want to reuse the cache.
[07:18] Daniel: KV cache is supported and the runtime manages it — you can pin contexts and the cache can be shared across requests in the same session to reduce tokens and latency. Key eviction policies are configurable.
[07:32] Tom: Security again — encryption at rest + in transit?
[07:36] Lina: TLS in transit, and data at rest encrypted with KMS. In Private deployments you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) to the HSM.
[07:45] Priya: Also need SSO and RBAC for console access.
[07:48] Maya: SSO via SAML/SCIM is supported; you can map roles to RBAC policies in the Console.
[07:55] [small pause] Daniel: I'm going to run a short scripted demo: submit a free-text doc, enforce schema, call validation tool, and show the trace.
[08:05] Daniel: Input: "Patient enrolled 12/06/2026, arm A: 50 mg, primary outcome: reduction in score by week 12" — send.
[08:18] Daniel: JSON Mode returns structured trial object, then runtime invokes validate_trial, which responded with status OK and no errors. Trace shows 144 tokens generated, 32ms validation call latency.
[08:30] Aisha: I noticed the schema had dates normalized. Good.
[08:33] Daniel: There's an optional normalization pipeline — you can plug converters for dates, units, etc.
[08:40] Tom: Are there any known failure modes where JSON Mode hallucinate fields?
[08:44] Daniel: Hallucinations are possible. We mitigate via: stricter schema, lower temperature, repair disabled in favor of explicit errors, and using deterministic fallback model. Also beat-in of parsing tools which validate fields against allowed vocabularies.
[08:59] Priya: For our legal review we need to ensure PII is scrubbed before any logs leave the VPC. Can we enable pre-log sanitizers?
[09:06] Lina: Yes — sanitizer hook runs before logs are emitted. You can configure patterns or call your internal scrubber function.
[09:17] Evan: Will the pilot require a full dedicated cluster immediately?
[09:21] Maya: No, pilot options: Hosted with strict routing to a pinned model for quick start, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable latency, or Private agent for compliance. Most customers start Hosted/Dedicated pilot then move to Private if needed. We'll recommend a small Dedicated pool for your test run.
[09:38] Tom: Cost estimate?
[09:40] Maya: We'll send a pilot estimate; high level: Dedicated monthly commit plus per-token for bursts. I'll include estimates in spreadsheet.
[09:48] [10:00 silence / notes]
[09:58] Aisha: A couple of quick edge questions — can we run schema-based evaluation on historical data?
[10:03] Daniel: Yes — you can run batch jobs via the Console or CLI to evaluate a corpus; Optimize will produce quality and token-cost reports.
[10:12] Priya: Anything we should ask legal about upfront?
[10:15] Maya: Yes — data residency, BYOK requirements, and whether the pilot can operate under a DPA addendum. We'll share our template.
[10:25] Tom: One last thing: we have an internal model stack we might want to plug as a fallback. How difficult is that?
[10:31] Daniel: Not difficult — you can register a local quantized model as a route target. The runtime supports GGML/ONNX quantized artifacts and will include them in the routing chain.
[10:40] Priya: Great. I'm happy with the audit/logging notes.
[10:44] Maya: Okay let's recap next steps — I'll email pricing and the pilot spreadsheet, Daniel will put together the benchmark plan, Priya will return compliance items, and Evan will share staging access if we go Private.
[10:56] Tom: Works for me.
[11:00] [meeting wrap] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invite for pilot kickoff.

End of transcript.
